Are you, then, willing to take a Solemn

source_text_or_hash: W. M. - I, A. B., in the presence of The Great Architect Of The Universe, and of this Worthy and Worshipful Lodge of Antient Free and Accepted Masons, lawfully constituted, and regularly assembled, of my own free will and accord do hereby (W.M. touches Can.’s right hand with his right hand) and hereon (W.M. touches the V.S.L. with his right hand and returns back to sign of fidelity) most solemnly and sincerely swear that I will always hele, conceal, and never wilfully reveal any or either of the secrets or mysteries of, or at all belonging to, Freemasonry, which shall now or may at any future time be communicated to me, to any individual whomsoever, except it be to one who has been properly proposed, and duly elected and has been presented, a Candidate properly prepared to be made a Freemason, and then only in the body of a Lodge Just, Perfect, and Regular. I further solemnly promise that I will not write those secrets, indite, carve, mark, engrave, or otherwise them delineate, or cause or suffer the same to be so done by others, if in my power to prevent it, upon anything movable or immovable, whereby or whereon any letter, character or figure, or the least trace of any letter, character or figure, may become legible or intelligible, so that our Secret Arts and Hidden Mysteries may improperly become known through my unworthiness. These several points I solemnly swear to observe, without evasion, equivocation, or mental reservation of any kind, in the certain knowledge, that on the violation of any of them, I shall be branded as a wilfully perjured individual, void of all moral worth, and totally unfit to be received into this or any other warranted Lodge, or any society of men who prize Truth and Honour above the external advantages of rank and fortune. So help me God, and may He keep me steadfast in this the great and Solemn Obligation of an Entered Apprentice Freemason. (W.M. removes the Compasses from the Can.’s left hand while Can.’s right hand remains on the V.S.L.)

source_text_or_hash: By your very decorous behaviour this evening you have escaped two great dangers, namely, those of stabbing and strangulation; for at your entrance into the Lodge, this Poniard (W.M. shows poniard) was presented to your naked left breast so that if you had rashly attempted to rush forward you might have been accessory to your own death by stabbing while the Brother who held it would but have remained firm and have done his duty. That Cable Tow also (shows cable tow) , with a running noose was placed about your neck so that any attempt to retreat might have been equally fatal by strangulation. But there is a third danger which will await you to the latest period of your life, namely, that on any violation of your Obligation, you will be branded as a wilfully perjured individual, void of all moral worth, and totally unfit to be received into this, or any other warranted Lodge, or any society of men who prize Truth and Honour above the external advantages of rank and fortune.

source_text_or_hash: W. M. - Now that you have taken upon you the Great and Solemn Obligation of an Entered Apprentice Freemason, I am permitted to inform you that there are several degrees in Freemasonry, with peculiar Secrets restricted to each. These, however, are not communicated indiscriminately, but are conferred upon Candidates according to merit and ability. I will now proceed to intrust you with the Secrets of this Degree, comprising the signs by which Freemasons are known to each other, and are distinguished from the rest of the world. But I will premise for your general information that all Squares and Perpendiculars (when applied to the position of the Body and its Limbs ) are true and proper Signs by which to know a Freemason. You are therefore expected to stand perfectly erect, with your feet in the form of a Square (W.M. shows Can. and he does the same); your body in its erect posture being an emblem of the uprightness of your mind, and your feet in their rectangular position being symbolical of the rectitude of your actions. You will now take a short pace forward with you left foot, bring the right heel into its hollow. That is the First Regular Step in Freemasonry, and it is in this position that the Secrets of this Degree are communicated. They consist of a Sign, a Grip or Token, and a Word. The Sign is given thus - (W.M. demonstrates) You will place your right hand in this position with the thumb extended in the form of a square to the left of the windpipe. The sign is given by drawing the hand smartly across the throat and dropping it to the side. (Can. copies) This is called the Penal Sign, it alludes to the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in the Obligation in this degree and implied that as a man of honour and an Entered Apprentice Freemason you would rather have had your throat cut across, your tongue torn out by the roots and your body buried in the sands of the sea, at least a cable length from high water mark where the tide regularly ebb and flow twice in the course of a natural day, than improperly divulge the Secrets of this degree. The Grip or Token is a distinct pressure of the thumb on the first knuckle of the hand. To this Grip a Word is attached, one highly prized among Freemasons, as a guard to their privileges. Too much caution cannot, therefore, be observed in communicating it. You must never give it at length, but always by, lettering or halving it, except in open Lodge. Being now in open Lodge, I will, for your instruction, give the Word in full. It is BOAZ. (W.M. spells it) As you will shortly be called upon for this Grip and Word, the Junior Deacon will now give the answers which you will then have to repeat for yourself.

source_text_or_hash: Bro. A. B., by the Worshipful Master's command, I invest you with the distinguishing Badge of an Entered Apprentice Freemason. It is more antient than the Golden Fleece or the Roman Eagle, more honourable than the Garter, or any other Order in existence, being the Badge of Innocence and the Bond of Friendship; and I strongly exhort you always to wear and to consider it in that character. You will observe that this Apron is made from the skin of a Lamb, and, as the Lamb has been from time immemorial the universally acknowledged emblem of Purity and Innocence, you will be thereby reminded of the purity of life and actions which should always distinguish a Freemason, and which is most essential to your gaining admission to that Grand Lodge above, where the blessed ever rest in eternal peace. We trust that you may live many years to wear that Badge, with pleasure to yourself, with usefulness to the Craft, and with honour to the Lodge in which you have been initiated; and let me further exhort you never to disgrace that Badge, for be assured that it will never disgrace you. I will add that you are never to put on that Badge and to enter a Lodge where there is a Brother against whom you may entertain any feelings of animosity. In such a case, it is expected that you will invite him to withdraw, in order that you may settle your differences amicably; which having been happily effected, you may then clothe yourselves and enter the Lodge, and work together with the love and harmony which should always characterise Freemasons. But if, unfortunately, your differences should be of such a nature as not to be so easily adjusted, it were better that one or both of you should retire, rather than that the harmony of the Lodge should be interrupted by your presence. source_text_or_hash: You now stand to all external appearance a just and upright man and Freemason; and I earnestly exhort you always to act up to that character. Indeed, I shall immediately proceed to put your principles in some measure to the test, by calling upon you to exercise that virtue which may justly be denominated the distinguishing characteristic of a Freemason's heart, namely, Charity. I trust I need not here dilate upon its excellences; doubtless it has often been felt and practised by you; it will be sufficient for me to say that it has the approbation of Heaven and of Earth: and, like its sister, Mercy, it bestows a double blessing:

source_text_or_hash: In a Fraternity so widely extended as Freemasonry is, having its branches spread over the whole habitable globe, it cannot be denied that we have many Brethren of rank and opulence among us; neither, on the other hand, can it be concealed that among the thousands who range under its banners, there are many who, perhaps from circumstances of unforeseen misfortune or calamity, are reduced to the lowest state of poverty and distress. In their behalf it is our usual custom to awaken the sympathies of every newly-initiated Brother, by making such a claim upon his Charity as his position and circum- stances in life may fairly warrant; anything therefore that you may feel disposed to give towards the relief of your distressed Brethren you may deposit with the Junior Deacon; and I assure you it will be thankfully received and faithfully applied.

Believe me, this trial was not made in order to sport with your feelings; far from us be any such intention. It was made for three especial reasons: firstly, to put your principles in some measure to the test; secondly, to evince to the Brethren that you had neither money nor metals of value about you, for, if you had, the Ceremony thus far must have been repeated; and thirdly, as a warning to your own heart, that should you at any future time meet a distressed Brother who may claim your assistance, and whom upon inquiry you may find to be deserving of assistance - not otherwise you would think upon the peculiar occasion when you were admitted into Freemasonry, poor and penniless, and would cheerfully embrace the opportunity of practising on his behalf the virtue of Charity, which in your present impecunious condition you are prevented from doing.

Indeed, no Institution can boast a more solid foundation than that upon which Freemasonry rests, namely, the practice of every moral and social virtue; and to so high an eminence has its credit been advanced that monarchs in every age have been promoters of the art, have not thought it derogatory to their dignity to exchange the sceptre for the gavel, have patronised our mysteries, and have joined in our assemblies.

source_text_or_hash: As a Freemason, I would first recommend to your serious study the volume of the Sacred Law, charging you to consider it as the unerring standard of truth and justice, and to regulate your actions by the Divine precepts which it contains; therein you will be taught the important duties you owe to God, to your neighbour and to yourself.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To God, by never mentioning His name but with that awe and reverence which are due from the creature to his Creator, by rendering to Him the tribute of praise and thanksgiving, for His manifold and great mercies and blessings; by imploring His aid upon all your lawful undertakings, and by looking up to Him in every emergency for comfort and support.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: To your neighbour, by acting with him upon the Square, by rendering to him every kind office which justice or mercy may require, by soothing his afflictions, by relieving his necessities, and by doing unto him in all things as in similar cases you would wish that he should do unto you.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: And to yourself, by such a prudent and well-regulated course of discipline, as may best conduce to the preservation of your corporeal and mental faculties in their fullest energy, thereby enabling you to employ those talents wherewith God has blessed you, as well to His glory as to the welfare of your fellow-creatures.

source_text_or_hash: As a Citizen of the World, I have next to enjoin you to be exemplary in the discharge of your Civil Duties, by never proposing or at all countenancing any act which may have a tendency to subvert the peace and good order of Society; by rendering due obedience to the laws of this, or of any other Kingdom or State, which may for a time, or in permanence, become the place of your residence or may afford you its protection; and above all by an unwavering allegiance to the Sovereign of your Native Land, ever remembering that nature has implanted in the breast of man a sacred, and it should be an indissoluble, attachment to the country from which he derives his birth and his infant nurture. As an Individual, I would further recommend to you the practice of every Domestic as well as public Virtue : let Temperance chasten you, Fortitude support you, Prudence direct you, and Justice be the guide of all your actions; being at all times especially careful to maintain in unsullied brightness that truly Masonic Jewel which has been already amply illustrated, namely, Charity.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Still, as a Freemason, there are other excellences of character to which your attention may be peculiarly and forcibly directed. Among the foremost of these are Secrecy, Fidelity, and Obedience. The Secrecy required of you is an inviolable adherence to the O... which you have entered into, never improperly to divulge any of those Masonic Secrets which have now been, or may hereafter be, communicated to you, and carefully to avoid all occasions which may inadvertently lead you to betray them.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: Your Fidelity must be exemplified by a close conformity to the Constitutions of the Fraternity, by adhering to the Antient Landmarks of the Order, by never attempting to extort or to otherwise improperly obtain the Secrets of a Superior Degree, and by refraining from recommending anyone to participation in the

source_text_or_hash: Your Obedience must be proved by a strict observance of our Laws and Regulations, by prompt attention to all Signs and Summonses, by modest and correct demeanour in the Lodge, by abstaining, while there, from every topic of religious or political discussion, by a ready acquiescence in all Votes and Resolutions duly passed by a majority of the Brethren, and by a perfect submission to the will of the Master and the Wardens of the Lodge, when acting in the discharge of the duties of their respective offices.
disposition: retained; structural headings may be consolidated

source_text_or_hash: And as a last general recommendation, let me exhort you to dedicate yourself to such pursuits as may enable you to become at once respectable in life, useful to mankind, and an honour to the Fraternity of which you have this day been admitted a member. That you will more especially cultivate such of the Liberal Arts and Sciences as may lie within the compass of your attainment; and that without neglecting the ordinary duties of your station in life, you will feel yourself called upon to make a daily advancement in Masonic Knowledge.

source_text_or_hash: From the exemplary manner in which you have conducted yourself during the Ceremony of your Initiation, and from the very commendable attention you have given to this Charge, we are led to hope that you will duly appreciate the value of Freemasonry, and that there may be indelibly imprinted upon your heart the sacred principles of Truth, of Honour, and of Virtue. M. - I will now explain the reasons for your preparation which at first sight, to your untaught mind, must have appeared somewhat strange; but every part of which has a deep symbolic import and is meant to convey an instructive and useful lesson. Preparation is of two kinds; internal and external. Internally you were prepared in your heart by a favourable impression preconceived of the Institution, a general desire for knowledge and a sincere wish founded on worthy motives to be ranked among its members, thereby enabling you to render yourself more extensively serviceable to your fellow creatures.

source_text_or_hash: Externally you were prepared in a convenient room adjoining the Lodge by having certain portions of your apparel arranged in a peculiar manner to prepare you for the ceremony of your initiation. You were hoodwinked or blindfolded. This was symbolic of your being in a state of darkness respecting the secrets of Freemasonry and to teach you to keep all others in a similar state of darkness until brought to the light; in the same regular manner as you yourself have been. Also that the mind must be made to conceive before the eye call be permitted to discover. A cable tow was placed about your neck, first as a means of restraint, should such have been necessary, and symbolic of your being in a state of bondage, the bondage of ignorance. Your left breast was made bare in token of your fidelity, and to prove that you were not an imposter as to sex, for our rules forbid the admission of females into the order; also that you might be received on the point of a sharp instrument presented thereto and instructed in the usual lessons of fidelity. Your right arm was made bare in token of your sincerity and to prove that you had no weapon of offence or defence about you, for the principles of our order forbid the use of one and that, therefore, automatically renders the use of the other unnecessary. Your left knee was made bare in token of your humility. On it you knelt and in the presence of The Great Architect Of The Universe entered into a solemn obligation never improperly to disclose any of the secrets entrusted to you. You were divested of all money and metals of value. This was to impress upon you that in a Freemasons Lodge, a man is not esteemed on account of his worldly possessions, for therein all men are equal, meeting on the level and parting on the square. It has also reference to the fact that at the building of King Solomon's Temple, it is written "there was no sound of a metal tool heard throughout the building, for the stones were prepared in the quarries, the timbers in the forests, and placed in position with wooden mauls. Your right heel was slipshod. This was in allusion to an ancient custom at the ratification of a bargain or contract such as we find recorded in the 4th Chapter of Ruth, the 7th verse. Now this was the manner in former times in Israel concerning redeeming and concerning changing, for to confirm all things a man plucked off his shoe and gave it to his neighbour and this was a testimony in Israel.

I further solemnly promise to act upon the Square (here the W.M. touches the Square held by the Can.) as a true and faithful Craftsman, to answer signs, to obey summonses, and to maintain the principles inculcated in the First Degree. These several points I solemnly swear to observe without evasion, equivocation, or mental reservation of any kind, and I pray to The Grand Geometrician Of The Universe that he will keep me steadfast in this Great and Solemn Obligation of a Fellow Craft Freemason.

source_text_or_hash: W. M. - Now that you have taken the Solemn Obligation of a Fellow-Craft Freemason, I will entrust you with the Secrets of this Degree. That is the Second Regular Step in Freemasonry, (Can. and W.M. keep standing in the 2nd Regular Step) and it is in this position that the Secrets of this Degree are communicated. They consist, as in the First Degree, of a Sign, a Grip or Token and a Word with this difference, that the Sign in this Degree is Threefold or may be separated into three several Signs. The second is given thus : Throw up the left hand with upper arm horizontal from the shoulder to the elbow, and lower arm perpendicular from the elbow to the finger tips with the thumb extended in the form of a square. (W.M. instructs Can. to copy and both maintain the sign) It is called the H....... S... or S... of P............ This is said to have been the Sign used by Joshua when fighting the battles of the Lord ‘in the going down to Beth-horon’. In this position he spake those memorable words, ‘Sun, stand thou still upon Gibeon; and thou, Moon, in the valley of Ajalon. And the sun stood still, and the moon stayed, until the people had avenged themselves upon their enemies’. This is the P.... S... : imagine holding a sharp instrument with the thumb and the first finger of the right hand, make a cutting motion downwards over the heart, grab the heart out, throw it across and downward to the right side, and return the right hand to the breast as before. (W.M. instructs Can. to copy and then both maintain the sign) It alludes to the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in the Obligation in this degree and implied that as a man of honour and a Fellow-Craft Freemason you would rather have your left breast laid open (W.M. demonstrates as he explains and instructs Can. to copy in synchronisation.) and your heart torn therefrom and given as prey to the ravenous birds of the air or the devouring beasts of the field than willingly or knowingly violate the Solemn Obligation of a Fellow- Craft Freemason. Being now in open Lodge, I will, for your instruction, repeat the Word in full; it is J...... As you will shortly be called upon for this Grip and Word, the Senior Deacon will now give the answers which you will then be expected to give for yourself. source_text_or_hash: The Infallible Plumb-rule, which, like Jacob's Ladder, forms a line of union between Heaven and Earth, and is the criterion of Moral Rectitude and Truth, teaches us, that to walk with Humility and Uprightness before God, neither turning to the right hand nor to the left from the strict path of Virtue, is a duty incumbent upon every Freemason. Not to be an enthusiast, a persecutor, or a slanderer; or a reviler of Religion; neither inclining to avarice, injustice, nor malice; nor to envy; or contempt of our fellow-creatures, but giving up every selfish propensity which may tend to injure others, and to steer the Bark of Life over the rough Seas of Passion, without quitting the Helm of Rectitude, constitutes the highest degree of perfection to which human nature is capable of attaining. As the Builder raises his Column by the Level and the Perpendicular, so ought every Freemason to carry himself in this life; to observe a due medium between Avarice and Profusion, to hold the Scales of Justice with an equal Poise; to make every Passion and Prejudice coincide with the strict line of his Duty, and in every pursuit to have Eternity in view.

source_text_or_hash: W. M. - I, A.B., in the presence of The Most High and of this Worthy and Worshipful Lodge of Master Masons, lawfully constituted and regularly assembled, hereby (W.M. touches Can.’s right hand with his right hand) and hereon (W.M. touches the V.S.L. with his right hand and returns back to sign of fidelity) most solemnly and sincerely swear, that I will always hele, conceal, and never wilfully reveal any or either of the secrets or mysteries, of, or at all belonging to, this Third Degree in Freemasonry, denominated the Master Masons' Degree, to any individual whomsoever, except it be to one who has been regularly initiated into Freemasonry, and passed to the Second Degree, and after a full month's probation has been presented as a Candidate properly prepared and fully qualified to be admitted to this Degree, and then only in the body of a Master Masons' Lodge regularly opened upon the centre. I further solemnly promise to adhere to the principles of the Square and the Compasses as they are inculcated in the First and the Second Degree; and that I will observe and uphold the Five Points Of Fellowship in act as well as in word; that my Hand given to a Freemason shall be a sure pledge of Brotherhood; that my Feet shall travel - if necessary - through dangers and difficulties, to unite with his, in forming a base upon which we two, standing side by side, may figuratively represent a column of mutual defence and support; that my Knee bent in daily prayer to The Most High shall always remind me of a Brother's wants, and shall dispose my heart to succour him in his weakness, and to relieve his necessities, as far as may fairly be done without injury to myself or my connections; that my Breast shall be the safe and sacred repository of his secrets, when entrusted to me as secrets, save that murder, treason, felony, and all other offences contrary to the Ordinances of God, and the Laws of the Land, shall be always especially excepted; and finally, that I will maintain a Freemason's honour and will carefully preserve it as my own; that I will not injure or malign him myself; nor knowingly suffer others to do so, if in my power to prevent it, but on the contrary will boldly repel the slanderer of his good name, and will at all times, and in all ways, most strictly respect the chastity of those nearest and dearest to him, in the persons of his wife, his sister, and his child. These several points I solemnly swear to observe, without evasion, equivocation, or mental reservation. of any kind, and I pray to the Most High that He will keep me steadfast, in this, the Great and Solemn Obligation of a Master Mason.

source_text_or_hash: M. M. - Now that you have taken the great and solemn Obligation of a Master Mason, I will shortly proceed to subject you to that last and greatest trial, by which alone you can be admitted to participation in the Secrets of the Third Degree. But it is first my duty to direct your attention to retrospect of those Degrees through which you have already passed, by which you will be enabled the better to comprehend and to appreciate the connection of our whole system and the interdependence of its several parts. Your initiation into Freemasonry in a state of helpless Indigence was an emblematical representation of the entrance of all men upon this their mortal existence. It inculcated the useful lessons of natural equality and mutual dependence; it instructed you, in the active exercise of Charity - in administering relief and consolation to your fellow - creatures in the time of their affliction that it is in very deed and in truth ‘more blessed to give than to receive.’ But, above all, it taught you to bend with humility and resignation to the will of The

source_text_or_hash: Great Architect Of The Universe, and to dedicate your heart, thus purified from every baleful and malignant passion, and fitted for the reception of Moral Truth, Wisdom, and Virtue, to the service of God, and to the good of your fellow-men. Proceeding onward, and still guiding your steps by the Principles of Moral Truth, you were led in the Second Degree to contemplate the Intellectual Faculties, and to trace them, from their inception and development, through the paths of Heavenly Science, even to the Throne of God Himself. The Secrets of Nature and the Principles of intellectual and Scientific Truth were then permitted to be unveiled to your view. To your mind, thus cultured and matured by Virtue and Science, Nature herself presents one great and useful lesson more. She prepares you by contemplation for the closing hour of your existence; and when you shall have been conducted through the ‘manifold changes and chances of this mortal life,’ she finally instructs you how to die. This, my Brother, is the peculiar object of the Third Degree in Freemasonry. It invites us to reflect upon this awful subject, and teaches us to feel that to the just and upright man Death has no terrors equal to the stain of falsehood and dishonour. Of this great truth the Annals of Freemasonry afford a glorious example in the unshaken fidelity and noble - of an antient Grand Master of our Order Hiram Abif who was treacherously and cruelly slain, shortly before the completion of King Solomon Temple in the designing and construction of which he was - as our traditions inform us - the chief architect. In order that you may be enabled to ‘comprehend and to appreciate’ the remaining portion of the Ceremony, I will explain to you the meaning of the word Abif which I have just used in connection with the name Hiram. It is a Hebrew word signifying ‘the son of a widow.’ It is recorded in the Volume of the Sacred Law that, in accordance with the request of King Solomon, Hiram, King of Tyre, sent to him a man who was well skilled in all details connected with ‘the erection of stately and superb edifices,’ to assist King Solomon in designing, erecting, beautifying, and adorning the Temple at Jerusalem. This man is described in the Volume of the Sacred Law as ‘the son of a widow woman of Tyre,’ and his name, like that of the King of Tyre, was Hiram.

source_text_or_hash: W. M. - I will now narrate to you the circumstances which led to the assassination of the Grand Master Hiram Abif, the chief architect of the Temple, the first martyr to his fidelity as a Master Mason, of whom the annals of Freemasonry contain the record; and I will then describe to you the manner of his death, in accordance with the teaching of our Masonic traditions. Five Fellow-Crafts, of the Order of the Menatschim - that higher Order whose members were appointed to superintend the labours of those craftsmen and others who wrought in the building of the Temple - seeing that that great and holy work was nearly completed, and that they and their fellows were not yet admitted to participation in the secrets, and thereby entitled to the privileges, of the Third Degree, joined in a conspiracy to obtain those secrets by any means, even if it should be necessary to have recourse to violence. On the eve, however, of carrying their plot into execution, two of them relented (the 2 Deacons take one pace backward); but the remaining three, being of a more determined and ruthless character than the seceding two, still persevered in their atrocious design, in the prosecution of which they placed themselves respectively at the South (the J.D. takes one loud step forward and places himself facing North and at right angle to the Can.), the North (the S.D. takes one loud step forward and places himself facing South and at right angle to the Can.), and the East (the W.M. takes one loud step forward facing the Can.) entrances of the Temple, whither the Grand Master, Hiram Abif, had gone to offer up his prayers and thanksgiving to The Most High, as was his wonted custom at the hour of offering the Evening Sacrifice. His devotions being ended, he. attempted to return by the South door, where the first conspirator was posted, and who, for want of other weapon, had armed himself with a heavy Plumb-rule. Assuming a threatening demeanour (the J.D. places his left hand on the Can.’s right shoulder and assume a threatening stance by holding the plump rule high up and staring at the Can.), he demanded of the Chief Architect the secrets of the Third Degree, warning him that death would be the consequence of a refusal. But he, true to his Obligation, replied, that those Secrets were known but to Three in the world, namely, to Solomon King of Israel, to Hiram King of Tyre, and himself, and that without the consent and co-operation of the other two, he would not - and indeed could not - reveal them; but he assured him that diligence and patience would, in due time, entitle the worthy Craftsman to participation in those Secrets, but that for himself he would rather suffer death than he would improperly reveal them. This answer failing to satisfy his assailant, he struck a heavy blow at the head of the Grand Master, but missing his aim, the weapon glanced with such force upon his Right Temple (the J.W. strikes his own left hand with the Plump Rule over the Can.’s right temple. Immediately the J.D. kicks the back of the Can.’s left knee.), as to cause him to sink to the ground upon his Left Knee. Recovering from this shock (Can. is lifted up), he then made for the North door, where the second ruffian was posted, to whom he answered, as in the previous instance, with undiminished firmness, when the villain, who was armed with a Level, struck him a violent blow upon the Left Temple (the S.W. strikes his own left hand with the Level over the Can.’s left temple. Immediately the S.D. kicks the back of the Can.’s right knee.), which caused him to sink to the ground upon his Right Knee. Finding all hope of escape cut off at both these quarters (Can. is lifted up), the stricken man then staggered, faint and bleeding, to the East door, where the third conspirator was posted. On receiving a similar reply to his insolent demand - for even at this perilousmoment the firmness of the Chief Architect remained unshaken - the murderous ruffian, who was armed with a heavy Maul, struck him a violent blow full (the W.M. strikes the Can.’s forehead with the Heavy Maul) upon the Forehead which laid him lifeless at his feet. (the Can. is made to lie down in the ‘grave’.)

source_text_or_hash: W. M. - The Brethren will take notice that in the recent Ceremony, as well as in his present position, our Brother has been made to represent one of the brightest characters recorded in the annals of Freemasonry, namely, Hiram Abif, who during his active and useful life excelled in all the curious and masterly workmanship of his Craft; and by his death, which he nobly suffered rather than he would betray the Secrets entrusted to his keeping, he has left an example worthy of the imitation of Freemasons through all succeed- ing ages. This, we trust, will make such an impression upon his and your minds, that you will not fail to act with similar firmness if you should ever be placed in a similar position of trial.

source_text_or_hash: W. M. - Now that you have passed through the necessary preliminary ordeal, I will proceed to entrust you with the Secrets of this degree. You will first advance to me with the Step (the shortest possible, a few inches only), and the Sign of an Entered Apprentice. (Can. does so and W.M. responds likewise.) Now, again, as a Fellow-Craft. (Can. does so and W.M. responds likewise.) Retaining the Sign of a Fellow-Craft, you will now take another Short Pace as before. (W.M. instructs Can. and demonstrates by taking a short pace forward with his left foot and put the heel of the right foot into the hollow of the left foot. The Can. does accordingly.)That is the third Regular Step in Freemasonry; and it is in that position that the Secrets of the Third Degree are communicated. They consist, as in the First and Second Degrees, of Signs, Tokens, and Words. The Signs in the whole are five in number, corresponding therein with The Five Points Of Fellowship. Of these, three are ordinary and two are extraordinary. I will at this stage of the Ceremony communicate to you the three ordinary Signs of a Master Mason. Two of these are Casual, the third is the Penal Sign. The first Casual Sign is formed from the F.Cs. thus; by a simultaneous movement you drop the left hand into this position, elevating the right with the back of the hand to the face, shielding the eyes with the head turned over the right shoulder.(W.M. demonstrates and instructs the Can. to copy.) This is called the Sign of Horror, as though struck with Horror at some gruesome object at which you had been gazing. The second is given thus; keeping the body erect, bend the head slightly forward, and pat the forehead with the palm of the hand. (W.M. demonstrates and instructs the Can. to copy.) This called the Sign of Sympathy, as though in sympathy with the sufferings of another. The Third is the Penal Sign. It is given thus; by drawing the hand smartly across the body, dropping it to the side and recovering with the thumb to the navel. (W.M. demonstrates and instructs the Can. to copy.) It alludes to the Ancient and Traditional penalties at one time included in the Obligation in this degree, it implied that, as a man of honour and a Master Mason you would rather be struck in twain, (W.M. demonstrates and Can. copies the motion of the Penal Sign) and have your body burnt to ashes and those ashes scattered over the face of earth and water, by the four cardinal winds of heaven, so that no trace or remembrance of you should longer exist among men, and more particularly among Master Masons than improperly reveal any of the Secrets of this degree. The Grip or Token is the first of the Five Points Of Fellowship, which are thus given and illustrated: Hand to Hand, (W.M. takes Can.’s right hand with the lion-like grip) I greet you as a Brother; Feet to Feet, (W.M. places his right foot against Can.’s right foot)my feet shall travel, if necessary, through dangers and difficult- ies to assist you in your time of need; Knee to Knee, (W.M. places his right knee to touch Can.’s right knee) my knees bent in daily prayer to The Most High, shall always remind me of a Brother's wants; Breast to Breast, (W.M. places his left breast to touch Can.’s left breast) my breast shall be the safe and sacred repository of your lawful Secrets when entrusted to me as Secret; Hand over Back, (W.M. extends his left hand over Can.’s left shoulder, Can. do likewise over the W.M.’s left shoulder) I will maintain a Freemason's honour in his absence as I would if he were present. It is in this Position only, and even then in a whisper, except in open Lodge, that the Words of this Degree are communicated; they are Machaben and Machbinna ; these words signifying severally the Death of the Builder and the Builder is Slain. The Deacons will now conduct you to the Wardens for trial and probation. (W.M. releases the Can., returns him to the S.D. and goes back to his seat.)

source_text_or_hash: J. W. - I will now explain to you the Working Tools of this Degree. They are the Skirrett; the Pencil; and the Compasses. (J.W. shows implements as they are named.) The Skirret is an implement which acts upon a centre-pin, from which a line is drawn to mark out the ground for the foundation of the intended structure. With the Pencil the skilful Architect delineates the building in a draft or plan for the instruction and guidance of the workmen. The Compasses enable him to ascertain and determine with accuracy and precision the limits and proportions of its several parts. Those are the uses of these implements in operative masonry; but in this as in the First and Second Degrees, we, not professing to be Operative, but Free and Accepted, or Speculative, Masons, apply these Tools to our morals; and in this sense the Skirret points out to us that straight and undeviating line of conduct marked out for us in the Volume of the Sacred Law.

source_text_or_hash: The Pencil teaches us that all our thoughts, words, and actions are observed and recorded by the Most High, to Whom we must hereafter render an account of our conduct through life. The Compasses remind us of His unerring and impartial justice, in having accurately defined for our instruction the limits of good and evil; and that He will, either reward or punish us according as we have obeyed or disregarded His Divine commands. Thus the Working Tools of this Sublime Degree teach us to bear in mind, and to act according to, the Laws of our Divine Creator, in the hope that when we shall be summoned from this sublunary abode, we may ascend to that Grand Lodge above, where the World's Great Architect lives and reigns supreme. source_text_or_hash: S. W. - (to Can.) We discontinued the narrative of our Traditional History at that part of it which describes the manner of the Death of the Grand Master, Hiram Abif. A loss so important as that of the Chief Architect could not fail to be speedily and severely felt. The want of those plans and designs which had theretofore been regularly supplied through every department of the work, had given rise to grave apprehensions that some serious mischance must have befallen him. The Menatschim - who were the general Overseers of the work - deputed certain of the more distinguished of their number to crave an audience with King Solomon, and to acquaint him with the utter confusion into which the absence of the Chief Architect had plunged them, and at the same time to express to him their fears that to some dire calamity must be attributed his so sudden and mysterious disappearance. King Solomon thereupon ordered a general muster of the Craftsmen throughout the various departments, when three of the superior class were not to be found; and on the same day the two who had originally joined in the conspiracy went before the King, and made a full confession of all that they knew, up to the time of their withdrawing themselves from the number of the conspirators. The fears of King Solomon being awakened for the safety of the Chief Architect, he selected fifteen trusty Fellow-Crafts, and ordered them to go and make diligent search for the person of the Grand Master, and to ascertain if he were still or had suffered in the attempt to extort from him the Secrets of his superior Degree. Accordingly, a day having been fixed for their return to Jerusalem, they formed themselves into three Fellow-Craft Lodges, consisting of five each, and departed severally from the three entrances of the Temple. Many days were spent in fruitless search; indeed, one Lodge eventually returned to Jerusalem without having effected any discovery; but the Brethren of the Second Lodge were more fortunate, for on the evening of a certain day, they having suffered many privations and much personal fatigue, one of their number, who had rested himself in a reclining position, in order to assist his rising, took hold of a shrub under whose shade he had reclined, and which to his surprise came easily out of the ground. On a close examination of the spot he discovered that the surface had been recently disturbed; he therefore hailed his Brethren, and with their assistance he reopened the ground, and there discovered the body of the Grand Master, very indecently buried. They covered it up with all respect and reverence; and in order to mark the spot they placed a branch of acacia at the head of the grave and then hastened to com- municate the afflicting intelligence to King Solomon. He, when the first emotions of his grief had subsided, ordered them to return, taking with them a sufficient number of Brethren to assist them, and to raise the body of Hiram Abif and to convey it to Jerusalem, there to perform upon it such rites of sepulture as became his rank and exalted talents. At the same time he informed them that by his untimely death the Genuine Secrets of a Master Mason were for a time Lost ; he therefore charged them to be particularly careful to observe any Casual Sign, Token, or Word which might occur while they were engaged in performing this last sad office of respect to departed merit. They performed their task with the utmost fidelity, for, on reopening the grave, one of the Brethren, looking round, observed several standing in this position, as though struck with Horror (sign) at what they beheld; others, viewing the gaping wound still visible on his forehead smote their own thus in Sympathy (sign) with his Sufferings. Two of the Brethren then descended into the grave, and severally attempted to raise the body of the Grand Master by the Grip of an Entered Apprentice and a Fellow-Craft; but as the body had lain some days in the Grave the Flesh gave and Slipped. A third zealous and more expert Brother then descended and taking a Firm and Lion-Like hold on the Sinew of the Right Arm, he, with the assistance of the other two, succeeded in raising him on the Five Points Of Fellowship and while some looked on in speechless Grief, others more animated exclaimed, Machaben and Machbinna, these Words signifying severally the Death of the Builder and the Builder is Slain. These Casual Signs, Grip, and Words were duly reported to King Solomon, who whereupon ordered that they should serve to distinguish them and all Master Masons throughout the World, until time or circumstances should restore the genuine ones. It only remains for me to account for the Third Lodge of Craftsmen. They had pursued their researches in the direction of Joppa, and were meditating a return to Jerusalem, when, on passing the mouth of a cavern, they heard issuing therefrom sounds of lamentation and remorse. On entering to ascertain the cause, they found three men who appeared to answer the description of those who were missing, and who on being charged with the murder, and finding all chance of escape cut off, made a full confession of their guilt. They were then Bound and Led to Jerusalem, where King Solomon ordered them to immediate execution, a punishment which the heinousness of their crime richly merited. The Body of Hiram Abif was ordered to be Reburied near to, but without, the walls of Jerusalem. He could not be buried within the precincts of the Temple, nor even within the City, because during the forty years' wanderings of the Israelites in the Wilderness, they, by God's special command, buried their dead beyond (or outside) the limits of the Camp; and when they entered into the Promised Land, and dwelt in fenced cities, they always buried their dead without the walls of their several cities. The fifteen Trusty Fellow-Crafts who had assisted in searching and finding the body of the Grand Master and in bringing his murderers to justice, were ordered to conduct his obsequies, clothed in White Aprons as emblems of their innocence. The implements with which Hiram Abif was Slain are the Plump Rule, the Level, and the Heavy Maul. The Skull and Cross Bones the emblems of mortality, are intended to remind us of his Untimely Death, which took place about three thousand years after the date commonly assigned to the creation of the world. M. - You have already been put into possession of the three ordinary Sign of a Master Mason; I will now intrust you with the remaining two; but for your further instruction I will go through the whole five. The origin of this Sign was the gesture made by Hiram Abif when after the second blow he made his way from the North to the East Entrance of the Temple, when his distress and agony were so great that the sweat and blood stood in great drops upon his fore- head, and he used this Sign (P.M. demonstrates) as a temporary alleviation of his sufferings. There is another Sign of Grief and Distress said to be in use in certain countries on the Continent of Europe, and which may be useful to a Brother who may happen to be in danger or difficulty in any of those countries. It is given by Clasping the Hands together thus with the Palms outwards, the Hands raised to the Forehead and exclaiming aloud in the language of the country, ‘Come to my assistance, ye Sons of the Widow’ You have already been informed that Hiram Abif was the Son of a Widow of Tyre and as we all masonically claim brotherhood with Hiram Abif so we may all be designated Sons of the Widow.
